title: Palindrome Number

understand.question: Given an integer x, how do we check whether its decimal digits read identically forwards and backwards — ideally without converting x to a string?
understand.plainExplanation: Negative numbers like -121 cannot be palindromes because the minus sign is only on the left. For positive numbers, if you reverse only the RIGHT half of the digits until the reversed half catches up to the remaining left half, both halves will match!
understand.outputMeaning: true if x is a palindrome, otherwise false.
rules: All negative numbers (x < 0) are false because '-' has no matching '-' on the right.
Any positive number ending in 0 (like 10 or 120) cannot be a palindrome because no non-zero number starts with 0; only 0 itself is a palindrome.
Reversing only half of the digits completely avoids integer overflow.

terms.definition: Building reversedRight from the rightmost digits while shrinking x from the right until x <= reversedRight.
In odd-digit numbers like 12321, the center digit 3 lands at the end of reversedRight (123 vs 12), so comparing x == reversedRight / 10 ignores it.

example1.whyValid: Digits mirror around the middle 3: 1 matches 1, and 2 matches 2.

example2.whyEdgeCase: Trailing zero trap! If we did not reject x % 10 == 0 (for x != 0) upfront, half-reversal on x = 10 would reach x = 0 and rev = 1, where x == floor(rev / 10) (0 == 0) would falsely return true.

steps.title: Verify non-negative and non-trailing-zero guards
steps.description: 12321 >= 0 and 12321 % 10 != 0, so it passes the upfront guards. Start with x = 12321, rev = 0.

state.caption: Ready to reverse right half while x > rev.

steps.title: Pop right digits 1 and 2 -> x = 123, rev = 12
steps.description: Iteration 1: rev = 1, x = 1232. Iteration 2: rev = 12, x = 123. Since 123 > 12, run one more iteration.

steps.title: Pop middle digit 3 -> x = 12 <= rev = 123 -> match!
steps.description: Iteration 3: rev = 123, x = 12. Now x <= rev so stop! Check x == rev (false) or x == rev // 10 (12 == 12 -> true!). Return true.

approaches.name: Reverse Half of Digits
approaches.recommendedTradeOff: Runs in O(log10 n) time with O(1) extra space, converts no strings, and never overflows 32-bit integers.
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Reverse digits into rev until x <= rev, then check x == rev or x == rev / 10.
approaches.coreIdea: Reject negative numbers and non-zero multiples of 10 immediately. Then peel digits from x into rev until x <= rev.
steps: If x < 0 or (x % 10 == 0 and x != 0), return false.
Initialize rev = 0. While x > rev: rev = rev * 10 + x % 10; x = floor(x / 10).
Return x == rev or x == floor(rev / 10).
approaches.whyItWorks: Stopping when x <= rev guarantees we split even-length numbers in half (x == rev) and odd-length numbers with the middle digit at the end of rev (x == rev / 10).

complexity.variables: n = |x| (number of decimal digits is ~log10 n)

approaches.name: String Conversion + Two Pointers
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Convert x to a string and compare characters inward from both ends.
approaches.coreIdea: Turn x into text and verify s[left] == s[right] as left and right move toward the center.
steps: Use two pointers l = 0, r = len(s) - 1; return false if s[l] != s[r], otherwise return true.
approaches.whyItWorks: Characters of str(x) directly mirror the decimal digits in order.
approaches.whenToUse: Readable alternative when O(log10 n) string allocation is acceptable.
approaches.diagramNote: Converts 12321 to "12321" and compares characters from left and right inward.

diagram.caption: L and R step inward while s[L] == s[R].

approaches.name: Full Reversal in 64-Bit Integer
approaches.coreIdeaSummary: Reverse every digit into a 64-bit integer and compare with the original x.
approaches.coreIdea: For x >= 0, reverse all digits using a 64-bit accumulator so overflow cannot happen, then check rev == x.
steps: Copy orig = x, rev = 0 (64-bit). While x > 0: rev = rev * 10 + x % 10; x /= 10.
approaches.whyItWorks: Any 10-digit reversed 32-bit integer easily fits inside a 64-bit signed integer.
approaches.whenToUse: Simple math implementation when 64-bit integers are available.
approaches.diagramNote: Reverses all 5 digits into a 64-bit integer rev = 12321 and compares rev == orig.
